ideas.title: Icom Filed Four New VHF and UHF Digital Radios With the FCC: What the Paperwork Shows
ideas.why_now: Icom filed two VHF digital transceivers on Oct 14, then two UHF digital transceivers on Oct 20 and Oct 23, plus a VHF air band radio on Oct 8. Four matched filings in nine days looks like a product family. A filing is not a product yet, and the video should say so plainly.
ideas.angle: New angle on a past pitch: that pitch covered only the two VHF filings, and the matching UHF pair plus the air band unit now changes the story. Quick-turn edited video for the OPEN 2026-10-29 YouTube slot: walk through each filing, what the paperwork can and cannot tell us, and how this fits Icom's busy year (ID-5200 pricing and pre-orders, the X-026 concept). Cut a Short from the reveal.

ideas.title: Ham Radio Gift Guide 2026: Battery Cases, Solar Adapters and Radios at Every Price
ideas.why_now: Holiday shopping starts the week of Thanksgiving. The most discussed community post this week was advice to always buy the AA battery case for your radio, and portable power talk is rising.
ideas.angle: Host idea (James K8JKU) for the OPEN 2026-11-26 YouTube slot. New angle on the earlier gift guide pitch: organize by price tier, and give the cheap tier mostly to portable power (AA battery cases, solar go-bag adapters, travel batteries). The channel has not covered that topic in a year, and it suits the practical everyday ham. Top tier: the $999 ID-5200 and HF rigs. Name brands and prices in every segment.

ideas.title: CW on a Quansheng Handheld: We Tried the New Firmware
ideas.why_now: New community firmware lets an inexpensive Quansheng FM handheld send and receive CW, and a competitor podcast just interviewed the firmware author. Budget radio discussion is rising.
ideas.angle: Edited video for the OPEN 2026-11-12 YouTube slot. Flash the firmware on a Quansheng, make a CW contact on 2 meters, and show who it is for: new hams learning Morse without buying an HF rig. This ties back to the channel's Learning CW episode, and it is a fun, cheap weekend project.

ideas.title: RADE and JTTY Land on Budget Radios and Phones: The New HF Modes Episode
ideas.why_now: In the last week the rewritten zBitx software added FreeDV RADE1, RADE2 and JTTY, and an updated Android FT8 app added JTTY and POTA/SOTA activation support. Hams are asking what JTTY feels like on the air.
ideas.angle: Host idea (James K8JKU, 'Will RADE Be the Next SSB'), recorded 2026-11-03 for the OPEN 2026-11-05 podcast slot, with a non-question title. Earlier pitches were bench tests on the shack rig. The new angle: these modes are reaching low-cost kit radios and phones. Play RADE vs SSB audio, do a JTTY on-air demo, and talk through what it means for portable operators.

ideas.title: QRV App With Adam K2CAT: A New Tool for Getting on the Air
ideas.why_now: Host Jim N8JRD flagged the QRV app as news. Ham software and app videos are breaking out for competitors this month, and logging and software discussion is rising.
ideas.angle: Host idea (Jim N8JRD) for the OPEN 2026-11-19 YouTube slot. Keep it a screen-led walkthrough with Adam K2CAT on camera, not a talking-head clip: the problem the app solves, a live demo, and what is coming next. Use the app name prominently in the title, the way app videos that break out do.

ideas.title: Always Buy the AA Battery Case for Your Handheld
ideas.why_now: This was the most discussed piece of ham advice this week, and go-bag power Shorts are breaking out right now.
ideas.angle: Short, which needs no release slot. Post it the week of 2026-11-12 to warm up the gift guide. In under a minute: a dead OEM battery, the AA case clicked on, the handheld back on the air. Name the radio brand on screen.

ideas.title: HOA Lobbyists vs the Antenna Bill: Getting on the Air With Restrictions
ideas.why_now: This week's news reports that HOA lobbyists are making it a top priority to stop the antenna bill. Antenna fights with local governments are pulling big views for a competitor.
ideas.angle: Recorded 2026-12-01 for the OPEN 2026-12-03 podcast slot. Explain plainly what the bill would do and why HOAs oppose it. Then spend the second half on practical stealth and restricted-lot options listeners can use today. The tone stays encouraging, not angry. This is an exception to the weak own-antenna numbers, justified by the news hook and competitor results.

ideas.title: RTL-SDR on an iPad and an Android Phone: Decoding FT8 With No Radio
ideas.why_now: SDR discussion jumped sharply this month. New releases let an RTL-SDR run on an iPad without jailbreak and on Android, and new SDR++ plugins decode FT8, CW, RTTY and more.
ideas.angle: Edited video for the OPEN 2026-12-10 YouTube slot. New angle on the earlier RTL-SDR junk drawer pitch: go fully mobile. Plug a dongle into a tablet and a phone, then decode FT8 and CW with the new plugins. This gives new and licensing-curious hams a cheap way to hear HF digital activity. It is an exception on the data (competitor sample too small), justified by the discussion surge.
